as1-basic-concepts-physical-inorganic: Why is chlorine's relative atomic mass 35.45 when no chlorine atom weighs that?
as2-further-physical-inorganic-intro-org: When a cold pack goes cold, has the chemical inside lost energy or gained it?
as3-basic-practical-chemistry: Can a strong acid have a higher pH than a weak acid?
a21-further-physical-organic: Two glasses of a blue sports drink look the same. How could a beam of light tell which holds more dye?
a22-analytical-transition-metals-electro: How can a substance join in a reaction, change, and still come out unchanged at the end?
a21-acid-base-equilibria: Is water an acid or a base?
a21-aldehydes-and-ketones: Why does cyanide add across a carbonyl double bond but leave an alkene double bond alone?
a21-aromatic-chemistry: Benzene is drawn with three double bonds. So why doesn't it react like an alkene?
a21-carboxylic-acids: Swap one hydrogen for a carbon chain: why does a sour acid become a sweet-smelling liquid?
a21-derivatives-of-carboxylic-acids: Why does ethanoyl chloride fume in moist air, when ethanoic acid just sits in the bottle?
a21-enthalpy-entropy-and-free-energy: Why does perfume spread across a room but never gather back into the bottle?
a21-equilibrium: A sealed flask looks unchanging. Can you tell which way it will react?
a21-isomerism: Spearmint and caraway get their smells from mirror-image molecules. How can your nose tell them apart?
a21-lattice-enthalpy: No one can pull a salt crystal apart into gaseous ions and measure the energy. So how do we know the lattice enthalpy of NaCl?
a22-amines: Fish smells fishy because of amines. Why does a squeeze of lemon juice take the smell away?
a22-amino-acids: How can one small molecule react with both acids and bases?
a22-chemistry-in-medicine: How can you titrate a tablet that won't even dissolve in water?
a22-chromatography: Why do the dyes in one drop of ink travel different distances up the same strip of paper?
a22-electrode-potentials: How can you measure the voltage of half a battery, when a voltmeter needs two connections?
a22-nuclear-magnetic-resonance-spectrosc: An MRI scanner images your body by detecting hydrogen nuclei. What can the same effect tell a chemist about a molecule?
a22-polymer-chemistry: Why does making a polyester give off water, when making some other plastics loses no atoms at all?
a22-volumetric-analysis: How can a purple solution measure the iron in a tablet without any added indicator?
as1-bonding: Salt is made of charged particles. So why doesn't a salt crystal conduct electricity?
as1-formulae-equations-and-amounts-of-su: How many water molecules are in a single drop of water?
as1-halogens: Chlorine was a poison gas in the First World War. So why do we put it in our drinking water?
as1-qualitative-tests: A jar of white crystals has lost its label. How can a few test tubes reveal exactly which salt it is?
as1-redox: When iron rusts, does it gain or lose electrons?
as1-shapes-of-molecules-and-ions: Water and carbon dioxide both have three atoms. Why is one bent and the other straight?
as1-structure: Diamond and graphite are both pure carbon. Why does only graphite conduct electricity?
as2-alcohols: How does a breath tester detect alcohol?
as2-alkanes: A fuel made only of carbon and hydrogen burns in air. Where do the poisonous gases in its exhaust come from?
as2-alkenes: Why does an alkene take bromine's colour away in the dark, when an alkane needs light?
as2-equilibrium: Air is mostly nitrogen and oxygen, which can react to form NO. Why isn't the air turning into NO?
as2-formulae-and-amounts-of-a-substance: Mix 10 g of hydrogen with 10 g of oxygen. Which runs out first?
as2-group-ii-elements-and-their-compound: Why does barium fizz in cold water when magnesium, in the same group, barely reacts?
as2-halogenoalkanes: How does warm sodium hydroxide turn a bromoalkane into an alcohol?
as2-infrared-spectroscopy: Why does carbon dioxide trap heat, while nitrogen, most of the air, does not?
as2-kinetics: Why can a cloud of flour dust explode, when a heap of flour only smoulders?
as2-nomenclature-and-isomerism-in-organi: How can C₂H₆O be both a liquid and a gas at room temperature?
